failure: SKILL.md said '13-agent roster' after the team was trimmed to 10
root_cause: a count was hardcoded in prose instead of derived; a roster change did not propagate to the skill
guard: after any roster change, grep the skill for stale counts; the authoritative roster lives in references/roster.md, not in prose

failure: the run workspace was placed inside the repository it served (a state folder of a notes repository), where its working .md files would be walked and linted by the repository's checks
root_cause: did not account for the repository's tooling walking every markdown file in its tree
guard: the run workspace is always OUTSIDE any repository's tree (the session's scratch or outputs folder, else the system temporary directory); never write working .md files inside the repository being served

failure: dispatch.md told analysts to write lanes/lane-N.md, but every Research team agent's spec says 'persists nothing; returns X'
root_cause: the flow was modeled on the reference skill (whose agents write files) instead of the standing team (whose agents return their artifact)
guard: the standing-team agents RETURN their artifacts; brief them to return, never to write a file; only the lead persists draft.md as the blind-review target (references/roster.md)

input: validate this skill (then named develop) while its metadata.team names a team that does not exist (a deleted crew)
expected: the deterministic validator flags a metadata.team that does not resolve to a staffed roster
was: the validator never checked metadata.team, so a dangling team pointer passed its own gate silently
lesson: a skill's metadata.team, when present, must resolve to a staffed roster in the skill's agents/ or an agent home, and scripts/validate.py enforces it

input: package this skill (then develop.skill) and install it in the Claude app while the skill template manifest is still named templates/skill/SKILL.md
expected: the archive contains exactly one file named SKILL.md (the manifest at the skill root) and installs cleanly
was: the archive shipped two files named SKILL.md, the root one and the skill template whose frontmatter was the placeholder name: [skill-name], so the install failed
lesson: a skill contains exactly one file named SKILL.md, at its root; template manifests are named t-SKILL.md so they never collide, and scripts/validate.py rejects a second SKILL.md

input: publish a skill that dispatches a team, then install the .skill archive somewhere that has no copy of the team's agents
expected: the archive carries the team's roster and agents in agents/, so the skill runs with nothing beside it
was: Publish said it vendored the referenced agents, but the validator forbade an agents/ folder and the packager never copied one, so no published archive carried its team
lesson: a published skill carries its team in agents/: scripts/package.py vendors the roster and its members from the agent home, and scripts/validate.py accepts and checks the folder
